newsitem.title: INDIA: India SEBI sets change in new issue tradeable lots.
newsitem.headline: India SEBI sets change in new issue tradeable lots.

text.p: India's market regulator, the Securities & Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Friday said it had introduced an option for issuers to change their minimum marketable lot on the basis of its offer price.

"In order to encourage participation of small investors in highly-priced public issues and offers for sale, an option has been given to issuers and offerors to fix the minimum marketable lot on the basis of offer price..." SEBI said in a statement.
The move takes retrospective effect from July 29, SEBI said, and will also apply to offer documents still awaiting SEBI's approval.

The market regulator said that issuers can now fix a minimum tradeable lot of 100 shares if the offer price per share was upto 100 rupees, 50 shares if the offer price ranged between 101-400 rupees and 10 shares if the price was over 400 rupees, the statement said.
SEBI fixed a maximum tradeable lot of 100 shares in the offer price.
